description: When a statement carries MORE THAN ONE problem, live reports them in an order fixed by KIND, not by which item happens to come first: syntax error > invalid identifier > unknown function > argument type / arity / semi-structured. Frostlake reported whichever the plan-time walk reached first, so writing the same two problems in the other order changed the answer; the select list is now walked ONCE PER KIND - column references, then call names, then everything else - which is what makes the order independent of position. Every pairing here is therefore asserted BOTH WAYS ROUND. The last test is the guard that the ordering hides nothing: each of the outranked refusals still fires on its own, with its own sentence. Converted 1:1 from query/RefusalPrecedenceTest (now retired).

steps.sql: CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t (a INT, b BINARY(4), v VARCHAR(5), o OBJECT)
INSERT INTO t SELECT 1, TO_BINARY('AB'), 'x', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('k', 1)
SELECT nosuchfn(1), OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(a, 1) FROM t
SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(a, 1), nosuchfn(1) FROM t
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t (a INT, b BINARY(4), v VARCHAR(5), o OBJECT)
INSERT INTO t SELECT 1, TO_BINARY('AB'), 'x', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('k', 1)
SELECT nosuchfn(1), GREATEST(b, v) FROM t
SELECT GREATEST(b, v), nosuchfn(1) FROM t
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t (a INT, b BINARY(4), v VARCHAR(5), o OBJECT)
INSERT INTO t SELECT 1, TO_BINARY('AB'), 'x', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('k', 1)
SELECT nosuchfn(1), ABS(1, 2) FROM t
SELECT ABS(1, 2), nosuchfn(1) FROM t
SELECT nosuchfn(1), o || 'x' FROM t
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t (a INT, b BINARY(4), v VARCHAR(5), o OBJECT)
INSERT INTO t SELECT 1, TO_BINARY('AB'), 'x', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('k', 1)
SELECT nosuchfn(1), nosuchcol, OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(a, 1) FROM t
SELECT nosuchcol, nosuchfn(1) FROM t
CREATE OR REPLACE TABLE t (a INT, b BINARY(4), v VARCHAR(5), o OBJECT)
INSERT INTO t SELECT 1, TO_BINARY('AB'), 'x', OBJECT_CONSTRUCT('k', 1)
SELECT ABS(1, 2) FROM t
SELECT OBJECT_CONSTRUCT(a, 1) FROM t
